The test image shows soybean **pods** — one pod is cracked/split open revealing brown, dry content inside. Pod candidates: Anthracnose, Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Green_stem_disorder, Phomopsis, Phytophthora, Purple_Seed_Stain, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, White_Mold.

The split pod with brown interior content points strongly to Phomopsis or Anthracnose. Let me check a Phomopsis reference.

The Phomopsis reference shows dried/mature brown pods with discolored seeds — the test image has green pods, which doesn't match well.

The test image shows green, still-developing pods with one pod cracked/split open revealing brown interior content. This matches **Anthracnose** pod blanking, where mycelium fills the pod cavity and seeds appear brown, moldy, and shriveled while pods may still appear somewhat green externally.

Key observations:
- Green pods (not yet fully matured/dried)
- One pod split prematurely open
- Brown/dried content visible inside — consistent with pod blanking
- No white fluffy mold, no purple staining, no dark spots on pod exterior
